evals.prompt: Run a traceability review of the agonara intent layer (intent×intent — cross-role and inside-role slices).
evals.expected_output: A single Markdown findings file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ that reports the intent layer as clean (0 cross-role and 0 inside-role findings), backs that verdict with cited interlocking evidence, enumerates every story per file, and logs exactly the two known tensions as routed open questions rather than findings.
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by the intent layer-pair (e.g. 2026-06-03T1007Z-intent.md).
The file front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming the intent×intent layer-pair and the agonara project, and slices [cross-role, inside-role].

The front-matter inputs list the four intent-layer files (intent_learning_program_app.md, admin_user_stories.md, curator_user_stories.md, student_user_stories.md) each with its document version read from that file's own front-matter.
The Summary reports 0 cross-role findings and 0 inside-role findings (a clean verdict).

The clean verdict is supported by positive evidence: the cross-role section cites the interlocking corpus/student-state and membership-authority boundary passages with file:line, rather than merely asserting cleanliness.
The Inspected section enumerates all story IDs per file: INT-01 through INT-07, ADM-01 through ADM-15, CUR-01 through CUR-18, and STU-01 through STU-23.

An open question records the curator membership operation-vs-policy tension (CUR-14/CUR-17 perform invite/remove while the curator boundary disclaims defining membership policy) and routes it to a downstream layer (intent→ADR, e.g. ADR-006) instead of reporting it as a finding.
An open question records the self-join vs invitation join-mode taxonomy ambiguity (STU-18 vs STU-22), noting the product intent itself already flags it as open, instead of reporting it as a finding.
The reviewer reads only the four intent-layer files and does not read ADRs, specs, implementation plans, code, or tests.
The reviewer makes no edits to any source document, opens no PR, and creates no file other than the single findings file.
No false-positive findings are manufactured — in particular the Russian/English language difference between the product intent and the story bodies is not reported as a contradiction.

evals.prompt: Run an intent → ADR traceability review of the agonara Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace module using the per-module deterministic coverage matrix.
evals.expected_output: A complete per-module coverage matrix (~22 capability rows) for Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace — each row verdict-tagged with ADR evidence — with findings derived mechanically: 0 contradictions, CUR-09 and CUR-13 carried with cited ADR lines, and the INT-02/STU-07 confusing-neighbors concept-relation flagged as a finding (loss or uncovered).
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by intent-adr and the module (e.g. 2026-06-03T1127Z-intent-adr-corpus-curator.md).

The front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming the intent → ADR layer-pair, agonara, and the module Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace, mechanism: deterministic-coverage-matrix, and an inputs list giving the intent files with versions, ADR-010 and ADR-009 with status, and the module responsibility map.

A coverage matrix is the primary artifact: roughly 20-24 rows, one per owned capability, each carrying an explicit verdict (carried, deferred, uncovered, carried-with-loss, or contradicted) and either an ADR file:line evidence quote or 'none'.

The enumerated capabilities include the curation stories CUR-01 through CUR-13 (and exclude CUR-14 through CUR-18 as Program Membership) plus the corpus-content capabilities INT-01..INT-03, the accepted-content slices of INT-04..INT-06, and STU-06/STU-07/STU-09/STU-10.
There are 0 contradicted rows (no fidelity fail).
CUR-09 (coverage-gap discovery) is classified carried, citing ADR-010:52 (gap analysis owned by Curator Workspace) and/or ADR-010:76 (coverage gaps live outside accepted corpus until acceptance).
CUR-13 (pre-acceptance suggestion origin) is classified carried, citing ADR-010:80 (acceptance preserves provenance to source/candidate/draft/LLM-suggestion/rationale) and/or ADR-010:56.

The INT-02/STU-07 confusing-neighbors concept-relation is flagged as a finding — either carried-with-loss or uncovered — and is NOT marked carried and NOT treated as deferred, quoting the intent commitment (intent_learning_program_app.md:115 / student_user_stories.md:80) and ADR-010's closed accepted-entity enumeration (adr-010:48 / :75).

Every finding corresponds to a non-clean matrix row and every row has a verdict; no finding is reported that is not a matrix row, and no false positive is made (an explicitly deferred capability or an implementation detail the intent left open is not flagged).
Cross-module seam gaps (a capability owned by no single module, e.g. program discovery) are NOT reported here, since they belong to the cross-module ADR × ADR pass.
The Inspected section confirms ADR-010 and ADR-009 and the four intent files and the responsibility map were read.

evals.prompt: Run an ADR × ADR cross-module compatibility traceability review of the agonara ADRs.
evals.expected_output: An ownership matrix (one row per map Owns entry) plus a cross-module contract register over the 16 accepted ADRs and the responsibility map, finding the architecture cross-module compatible (0 double-ownership, 0 contract inconsistency, 0 boundary violation) with map-adr-drift the only finding category — including the accepted Program shell (ADR-009) not named in the map's Corpus Storage Owns cell.
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by adr-adr-crossmodule.

The front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming the ADR × ADR layer-pair and agonara, checks listing double-ownership / boundary-violation / contract-consistency / map-adr-drift, mechanism: ownership-matrix + contract-register, and an inputs list giving the module responsibility map with version and all 16 ADRs with status.

An ownership matrix is produced with one row per responsibility from the map's Owns columns, each row carrying the map owner, the ADR(s) that decide it with file:line, and a verdict (single-owner, double-ownership, or map-adr-drift).

A cross-module contract register is produced, each row naming a contract with its provider ADR (file:line) and consumer ADR(s) (file:line) and a verdict (consistent, inconsistent, or boundary-violation).
There are 0 double-ownership rows in the ownership matrix.
The contract register has 0 inconsistent and 0 boundary-violation rows (every cross-module contract is consistent).
There are 0 fail findings, and the only finding category present is map-adr-drift (warning).
A map-adr-drift finding flags that the accepted Program shell owned by Corpus Storage per ADR-009 (adr-009:44) is not named in the map's Corpus Storage Owns cell (module_responsibility_map.md:68).

The identified shared contracts include at least the effective-participation authorization contract (provider ADR-007, consumed by Student/Curator/Admin) and the curator-acceptance boundary (ADR-010), each verdict consistent with provider and consumer file:line.
No intents, specs, plans, code, or tests are read, and seam coverage (a capability owned by no module) is explicitly noted as out of scope for this pass.
The Inspected section confirms the responsibility map and all 16 ADRs (adr-001 through adr-016) were read.

evals.prompt: Run the allocation-completeness pass on agonara — is every intent capability owned by at least one module?
evals.expected_output: A complete global allocation matrix (one row per intent capability) over the intent layer, responsibility map, and 16 ADRs, finding the architecture allocation-complete (0 unallocated capabilities), with the program-discovery capabilities STU-01/02/03 classified allocated and the suppression rules preventing false positives (deferred-mechanics and cross-cutting concerns not flagged).
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by intent-allocation.

The front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming allocation completeness and agonara, mechanism: global-allocation-matrix, a suppression_rules list, and an inputs list giving the four intent files with versions, the responsibility map with version, and all 16 ADRs with status.

An allocation matrix is the primary artifact: one row per intent capability covering INT-01..07, ADM-01..15, CUR-01..18, STU-01..23 plus cross-cutting concerns, each row carrying owner(s) with module + ADR/map file:line (or none), an owner_count, and a verdict (allocated, cross-cutting-allocated, deferred, pending, or UNALLOCATED).
There are 0 UNALLOCATED rows (the architecture is allocation-complete).
STU-01 (see available programs) is classified allocated, owned by Corpus Storage's accepted Program shell (ADR-009).
STU-02 (see started programs) is classified allocated, owned by Program Membership (membership status / effective participation, ADR-005/ADR-007).
STU-03 (preview coverage) is classified allocated, owned by Corpus Storage (accepted-content read / answer-key-excluding delivery projection, ADR-010/ADR-016).

The suppression rules prevent false positives: a cross-cutting concern with no dedicated ADR (e.g. Product Analytics) is resolved via a system-level owner in the map rather than flagged UNALLOCATED, and a capability whose owner is explicit but whose mechanics are deferred by ADR Non-Goals (e.g. CUR-09 gap analysis owned by Curator Workspace) is allocated, not a finding.
ADRs are treated as authoritative over the provisional responsibility map for ownership, and an ADR Non-Goal is the authority for a deferred verdict.
No false UNALLOCATED finding is made — a deferred, cross-cutting, or owner-explicit capability is never flagged as owned-by-nobody.
The Inspected section confirms the four intent files, the responsibility map, and all 16 ADRs were read.

evals.prompt: Run the ADR → spec pass on the agonara Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace module — does the spec honour every ADR-010 decision?
evals.expected_output: A complete per-decision matrix over ADR-010 and its two corpus-acceptance specs, finding the specs faithful (0 contradicted, 0 missing) with the broad content-kind set correctly classified deferred (not missing) under the ADR's narrow-first-implementation allowance.
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by adr-spec and the module (corpus-curator).

The front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming the ADR → spec pass, the Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace module, and agonara, mechanism: per-decision matrix, and an inputs list giving adr-010 (status) and both corpus-storage-and-curator-acceptance specs (api + first-slice) with version/status.

The matrix is the primary artifact: one row per ADR-010 decision / rule / invariant (pinned to the ADR's own Decision and Rules sections), each row carrying a verdict (honoured, contradicted, missing, or deferred) and either a spec file:line evidence citation or 'none'.
There are 0 contradicted rows (no fail).
There are 0 missing rows, so 0 findings total.
Honoured rows cite concrete spec evidence with file:line (e.g. the 'draft rejection MUST NOT delete accepted corpus' invariant at adr-010:85 maps to a first-slice spec rule).

The broad content-kind set (ADR-010 at :48/:75 owns topics, concepts, definitions, principles, material references, source metadata, accepted assessment items, and criteria) where the first slice realizes only topic/concept is classified deferred (not missing), citing adr-010:102 (narrow first implementation) and/or Non-Goal adr-010:109, and routed as an open question for a later spec slice — not reported as a gap.
Admin recovery (R23, adr-010:87 'later ADR-defined exceptional flow') and the later-ADR extension clause (adr-010:88) are classified deferred, not findings.
Findings are derived mechanically from the matrix and no false positive is made — a narrowing authorized by an ADR Non-Goal or first-slice scoping line is deferred, never flagged missing.
The Inspected section confirms ADR-010 and both corpus-storage-and-curator-acceptance specs were read.

evals.prompt: Run the spec ↔ tests pass on the agonara Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace module — does every spec clause have a named test, and does every test name trace to a clause?
evals.expected_output: A bidirectional coverage matrix (spec clauses ↔ test names) for the module, built from test titles only (no bodies, tests not run) with the test scope discovered across the whole suite, finding coverage clean (no orphan tests; negative-guarantee verifiability noted as an open question, not a forced untested finding).
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by spec-tests and the module (corpus-curator).

The front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming the spec ↔ tests pass / the Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace module / agonara, a mechanism noting bidirectional coverage by names only, and an inputs list giving both corpus-storage-and-curator-acceptance specs and the test files used.
Spec clauses are enumerated from BOTH specs (first-slice + API) as the clause set.

The test scope is discovered across the whole test suite (not a single hand-listed file): corpus/curator-relevant titles are drawn from wherever they live — domain corpus*.test.js, API http-api.test.js, backup-restore.test.js, executable-acceptance — and titles for other modules are classified out-of-scope, not orphan.
Coverage is bidirectional: a Spec->test table (each clause -> covering test name or untested) and a Test->spec table (each in-scope test name -> traced clause or orphan).
Only test NAMES are used (describe/it/test titles, e.g. grep-extracted); test bodies are not analyzed and the tests are NOT run.
There are 0 orphan tests (every in-scope test name traces to a clause).
Forward coverage is essentially complete (clauses covered by named tests) with no contradicted/false-coverage rows.
A negative or does-not guarantee clause that no test names is treated as an open question (names-only cannot confirm an absence), not a forced untested finding.
A clean result is backed by the completed bidirectional tables, not asserted, and the Inspected section lists the specs and test files consulted.

evals.prompt: Run the upward orphan check on the agonara Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace module — does every ADR-010 and ADR-009 decision trace back to a source intent, or is any unrequested scope creep?
evals.expected_output: A complete upward-trace matrix (one row per ADR-010 and ADR-009 Decision sentence and Rules/Invariants bullet) over the two ADRs and the intent layer, finding 0 orphans — every decision traced to an accepted intent or classified as a legitimate derived/carried-shape decision — with the parent-less-looking decisions (Program shell + operator-visible metadata, self-join admission default, stable accepted revisions, acceptance attribution/event emission) caught by the suppression guards and the genuinely intent-deferred specifics routed as open questions rather than flagged ORPHAN.
expectations: The output is a single new Markdown file under agonara/docs/traceability-reviews/ whose name is a UTC timestamp followed by orphan and the layer/module (e.g. 2026-06-03T1928Z-orphan-adr-intent-corpus-curator.md).

The front-matter includes skill: traceability-review, a skill_version, scope naming the upward orphan check / ADR → intent / the Corpus Storage + Curator Workspace module / agonara, mechanism: upward-trace-matrix, a suppression_rules list, and an inputs list giving adr-010 and adr-009 with status, the four intent files with versions, and the responsibility map with version.

An upward-trace matrix is the primary artifact: one row per ADR-010 and ADR-009 Decision sentence and Rules/Invariants bullet (pinned to the ADRs' own units — Executive Summary, Context, Consequences, and Non-Goals are NOT enumerated as rows, and rules are neither sub-split nor folded), each row carrying a verdict (traced, derived, carried-shape, or ORPHAN) and a cited parent: an intent ID file:line for traced, the derivation/elaboration parent, or 'none — ORPHAN'.
There are 0 ORPHAN rows — the module is orphan-free.

The verdict is backed by the completed matrix with both sides cited (intent file:line and adr file:line), not asserted; the row total is reported as approximate (ADR prose decisions carry no stable IDs) and the eval does NOT require an exact row number.

The Program shell decisions (ADR-009: a minimal accepted Program record with a stable identifier and operator-visible metadata) are NOT flagged ORPHAN — classified derived or carried-shape because CUR-01/INT-01 commit that a program exists and the shell is the minimal stable scope the intent left to design, with the operator-visible-metadata clause routed as an open question (resolving layer: intent).

The self-join admission default (ADR-009) is NOT flagged ORPHAN — classified carried-shape of STU-18 (which commits self-join's existence), with the specific default routed as an open question because the intent explicitly leaves admission policy open.

Stable accepted revisions and addressability (ADR-010) are NOT flagged ORPHAN — classified derived/carried-shape because CUR-10 and INT-07 require that corpus evolution not erase student history, which the revision mechanism honours.

Acceptance attribution, provenance, atomicity, and event-emission rules are NOT flagged ORPHAN — classified derived as internal integrity/provenance primitives serving traced acceptance and membership decisions (and ADM-15 audit), never user-observable scope creep.

No false-positive ORPHAN is manufactured: a decision with a derivation chain to a traced decision or a system-level need, or one elaborating an intent-left-open capability, is derived/carried-shape, not ORPHAN; the derived-vs-orphan disposition is left to judgement (the eval does not pin the traced/derived split).
Only the two ADRs, the four intent files, and the responsibility map are read; no specs, plans, code, tests, or prior review outputs are read, and no source document is edited.
The Inspected section confirms ADR-010 and ADR-009 (decisions enumerated), the four intent files, and the responsibility map were read.
